messages:
Maya: Quick Q - planning a small contract change for the embeddings endpoint. Proposal: keep empty-string inputs as valid items and return a zero-vector (shape preserved) instead of dropping/omitting them. This avoids index shifts in batched responses. Ping for opinions before I open the PR.
Sam: +1 from infra — dropping causes partial failures downstream, we see index misalignment in search pipelines.
Alex: Curious about how we represent zero-vector: all zeros or sentinel? Prefer all-zero float vector to keep numeric type consistent.
Priya: Also need to confirm behavior for null vs missing. Current SDKs coerce undefined/empty -> null. We should document explicitly.
Jon: Backcompat: older clients expect removal of empty items (they treated them like blanks). Doing this is a breaking change for them. Suggest opt-in header first: X-Embed-Preserve-Empty: true
Maya: Good point. Alternative: preserve by default but add a compatibility flag? Which is safer?
Sam: Safer to opt-in for now. We'll roll it canary for 24h on dedicated infra.
Priya: Implementation details: if preserved, output vector length must match model dims. I'll add unit test with shape check. Also need to ensure batching: max 512 items per request, and we must ensure memory accounting when lots of zero vectors are produced.
Maya: Proposed API notes:
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-v1",
  "input": ["", "hello world", "long text..."],
  "preserve_empty": true
}
```
Response example:
```json
{
  "data": [
    {"embedding": [0.0, 0.0, ..., 0.0]},
    {"embedding": [0.12, -0.03, ...]},
    {"embedding": [0.01, 0.44, ...]}
  ],
  "model_dim": "1024"
}
```
Maya: Notes: model_dim is added to avoid guessing dims. We should also return per-item warnings for truncated inputs and a code for partial failures.
Alex: Lgtm. Also add `items_processed` and `items_skipped` counters in response metadata.
Jon: If we go opt-in, API header is ok. We'll need compatibility tests for old SDKs. Can we bump minor version if default changes?
Priya: I'll open a tests PR + docs patch. Who wants the code review on platform side?
Maya: @Sam can you own the infra side (canary routing + quota)? @Alex can you review the runtime patch? I'll do the docs/SDK notes.
Sam: Yep, I'll put together canary plan. Can we schedule small window tomorrow 10:00 UTC for the rollout? Need oncall alerted.
infra-bot: deploy-plan created: canary group = 5% traffic (dedicated pools only), monitor latency and error-rate for 2h. Ping @oncall-team.
Maya: Thanks — will open PR now and include acceptance criteria: stable indexes, model_dim in response, header opt-in. Will tag reviewers.
Alex: Quick flag: ensure embedding arrays always length==model_dim, no sparse representations.
Priya: I'll add a policy doc entry about preserving empty inputs + examples.
Jon: Code review ping: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/2345
Maya: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Sam: adding to schedule. Oncall FYI @oncall-team
